# Sirach Chapter 31 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 31 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_031_page_001.jpg

---

**31:1** Sleeplessness over wealth wastes the body, and worry about it drives away sleep.

**31:2** Anxious worry cuts off slumber, and a serious disease carries off sleep.

**31:3** The wealthy man labors in accumulating riches, and when he rests he is filled with pleasures.

**31:4** The poor man labors in poverty of livelihood, and when he rests he is in want.

**31:5** Whoever loves gold will not be declared righteous, and whoever pursues money will be led astray by it.

**31:6** Many have been brought to ruin because of gold, and their destruction came before their faces.

**31:7** It is a stumbling block to those who sacrifice to it, and every fool will be ensnared by it.

**31:8** Blessed is the wealthy man who has been found without blemish, and who has not gone chasing after gold.

**31:9** Who is he? And we will call him blessed, for he has performed wonders among his people.

**31:10** Who has been tested by it and found perfect? Let that be his glory. Who was capable of transgressing and did not transgress, and capable of doing harm and did not do it?

**31:11** His prosperity will be established, and the congregation will proclaim his charitable deeds.

**31:12** If you are seated at a great man's table, do not open wide your throat over it, and do not say, "How much there is on it!"

**31:13** Remember that the evil eye is a wicked thing. What has been made more evil than an eye? Therefore it weeps from every face.

**31:14** Do not extend your hand to whatever it looks at, and do not jostle it in the dish with him.

**31:15** Judge your neighbor's feelings by your own, and be discreet in every matter.

**31:16** Eat like a well-bred person what is set before you, and do not devour food greedily, lest you be despised.

**31:17** Be the first to stop eating out of proper conduct, and do not be gluttonous, or you will give offense.

**31:18** And if you are sitting among many persons, do not reach out your hand before them.

**31:19** How sufficient is a little for a well-disciplined man! He does not pant upon his bed.

**31:20** Sound sleep comes with a disciplined stomach; he rises early and is at ease in himself. The agony of sleeplessness, nausea, and gripping pain attend the undisciplined man.

**31:21** If you have been compelled to eat too much, get up, go out, vomit, and you will have rest.

**31:22** Listen to me, my child, and do not disregard me; in the end you will appreciate my words. In all your activities be diligent, and no illness will overtake you.

**31:23** The generous man — people will speak well of him, and the testimony of his excellence is to be trusted.

**31:24** The miser — the city will complain of him, and the testimony of his meanness is reliable.

**31:25** Do not put yourself forward in wine-drinking, for wine has been the ruin of many.

**31:26** The furnace tests the work of the smith; so wine tests hearts when the proud are quarreling.

**31:27** Wine is life to human beings when drunk in moderation. What life is there for a man who lacks wine? For it was created to make people glad.

**31:28** Wine drunk with good judgment and in due measure brings joy to the heart and cheerfulness of soul.

**31:29** Wine drunk excessively leads to bitterness of temper, provocation, and stumbling.

**31:30** Drunkenness heightens the rage of a fool to his own hurt, diminishing his strength and adding wounds.

**31:31** Do not rebuke your neighbor during a wine-feast, and do not humiliate him during his celebration. Do not speak words of reproach to him, and do not press him with demands.
